title: Quasi-coherent algebra descent on affine action quotients
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and put $H=k[G]$, with comultiplication $\Delta$ and counit $\epsilon$. Let $D$ be any commutative $k$-algebra with a $k$-algebra coaction $\rho_D:D\to D\otimes_kH$ satisfying $(\rho_D\otimes1)\rho_D=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho_D$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho_D=1_D$. Let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra and $j:A\to D$ a $k$-algebra map whose image is invariant, meaning $\rho_D(j(a))=j(a)\otimes1$ for all $a\in A$. Define $\mathcal X=[\operatorname{Spec}D/G]$ by the torsor-and-equivariant-map formula of [def-sfb-affine-action-quotient-stack], allowing arbitrary $D$: over a $k$-scheme $T$, objects are left $G_T$-torsors $P\to T$ for the fppf topology equipped with an equivariant map $P\to\operatorname{Spec}D$, and arrows are equivariant torsor isomorphisms commuting with this map. All pullbacks, total arrows over base maps, identities, composition and the canonical atlas use the full formulas of that definition with $E$ replaced by $D$. To fix the left-action convention explicitly, let $S:H\to H$ be the Hopf antipode (pullback by group inversion) and $\tau:D\otimes_kH\to H\otimes_kD$ the factor swap. The associated left scheme action has coordinate map $a_D^*=(S\otimes1)\tau\rho_D$; equivalently, if the right coaction is written as a right scheme action $x\cdot g$, then $g\cdot x=x\cdot g^{-1}$. The same convention applies to $D_C$ and $B$. Then $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack in the sense of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and $j$ induces a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism $\psi:\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. For every commutative $A$-algebra $C$, put $D_C=D\otimes_A C$ with coaction induced by $\rho_D$ and the trivial action on $C$. There is a natural equivalence $\mathcal X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}C\simeq[\operatorname{Spec}D_C/G]$. Pullback to the atlas $\operatorname{Spec}D_C$ identifies quasi-coherent algebras on this stack [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] with commutative $D_C$-algebras $B$ carrying a $k$-algebra coaction $\rho_B:B\to B\otimes_kH$ satisfying the same counit and coassociativity identities, for which $D_C\to B$ is equivariant. This equivalence identifies surjections with surjective equivariant $D_C$-algebra maps, and identifies global sections of the algebra corresponding to $B$ with $B^G=\{b\in B:\rho_B(b)=b\otimes1\}$. These identifications commute with homomorphisms of algebras and restriction under further scalar extension. In particular, the structure sheaf has section ring $D_C^G$, and its structural map from $C$ is $c\mapsto1\otimes c$. Neither $D$, $C$ nor $B$ is required to be finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), applied to the affine action groupoid; groupoids.tex Tag 03LF (definition-equivariant-module). Algebraicity: algebraic.tex Tag 04TK (theorem-smooth-groupoid-gives-algebraic-stack). Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness: stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 050X (lemma-surjection-from-quasi-compact) and 075S (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence). Scalar extension is the torsor formula for the fibre product. Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3 Section 2.1 corroborates the coaction convention.

proof.text: Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$. Contravariance of affine spectra turns the counit and coassociativity equations into the identity and associativity laws for the right action $x\cdot g$. Inversion gives the stated left action $g\cdot x=x\cdot g^{-1}$, since $(x\cdot h^{-1})\cdot g^{-1}=x\cdot(gh)^{-1}$; its coordinate map is precisely $(S\otimes1)\tau\rho_D$. Form $R=G\times_kU$ with $s(g,x)=x$, $t(g,x)=g\cdot x$, identity $(1,x)$, inverse $(g^{-1},g\cdot x)$ and composition $((h,g\cdot x),(g,x))\mapsto(hg,x)$. The group laws give all groupoid identities on test schemes. The map $s$ is the base change of $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence smooth; inversion interchanges $s,t$, so $t$ is smooth as well.

source.place: Tag 03LF (definition-equivariant-module); action-groupoid construction, with the inverse convention fixed in the statement

proof.text: Apply the smooth-groupoid quotient theorem to $(U,R)$; it gives an algebraic stack with smooth surjective atlas $U$ and $U\times_{[U/R]}U=R$. Apply the torsor comparison, which explicitly permits arbitrary $U$, to identify this stack and atlas with the torsor formula in the statement. In particular no finite generation of $D$ has entered.

The morphism $u:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ induced by $j$ is invariant: the two coordinate maps of $u\circ s,u\circ t$ agree by $\rho_Dj(a)=j(a)\otimes1$ and $S(1)=1$. On an object $(P,f)$ over $T$, choose fppf local trivializations of $P$. They give maps from the covering schemes to $U$; their maps to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ agree on overlaps by this invariance. An fppf covering is fpqc, so representable descent gives a unique map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Uniqueness makes this assignment independent of trivializations and compatible with arrows and base pullback, giving $\psi$.

source.place: Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks), torsor description; invariance and descent of the structural map

proof.text: Any morphism between affine schemes is affine: its pullback by an affine test scheme is the spectrum of the tensor product of their coordinate rings, hence affine. In particular $U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine and therefore quasi-compact by affine-morphism permanence. $\operatorname{Spec}A$, as a discrete fibred groupoid, is an algebraic stack (fpqc descent of morphisms, identity atlas), so $\mathcal X\times_A\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack by the fibre-product theorem; this is needed for the locality theorem and the chartwise calculus below. The relative diagonal of $\psi$ is representable by algebraic spaces, since its scheme tests are the isomorphism spaces between two objects of the algebraic stack with a common $A$-map. Pulled back along $U\times_AU\to\mathcal X\times_A\mathcal X$, it is $R\to U\times_AU$, sending $(g,x)$ to $(x,g\cdot x)$. Both schemes are affine by the affine fibre-product formula, so this map is affine; its coordinate map is $D\otimes_AD\to H\otimes_kD$, $d\otimes e\mapsto(1\otimes d)a_D^*(e)$. The displayed cover is smooth and surjective (a composite of base changes of the atlas), hence flat and locally finitely presented. The representable fppf locality theorem proves that $\Delta_\psi$ is affine. Apply the qcqs atlas/diagonal criterion to conclude that $\psi$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 050X (lemma-surjection-from-quasi-compact), Tag 04YW (definition-separated); atlas computation of the relative diagonal

proof.text: For an $A$-algebra $C$, set $E=D_C$. The formula $\rho_E(d\otimes c)=\sum(d_{(0)}\otimes c)\otimes d_{(1)}$ is well-defined: the relation $dj(a)\otimes c=d\otimes ac$ is respected because $j(a)$ is invariant. Counit and coassociativity follow on these tensor generators. Over a $C$-scheme $T$, an object of the $2$-fibre product is $(P,f)$ together with its structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}C$; compatibility over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ says exactly that $f:P\to U$ and $P\to T\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ have the same $A$-map. The fibre-product property gives a unique equivariant map $P\to U\times_A\operatorname{Spec}C=\operatorname{Spec}E$. Conversely forget this lift. These operations are inverse on objects and arrows and commute with base maps; the atlas becomes $\operatorname{Spec}E$.

source.place: Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks), torsor formula under scalar extension

proof.text: By the torsor comparison for $V=\operatorname{Spec}E$, the torsor stack of the preceding step is the fppf stackification of the action groupoid on $V$, compatibly with pullback, so quasi-coherent algebras correspond under this equivalence. Apply module descent to this action groupoid. Using affine tilde/global-sections equivalence on $V$ and on the arrow scheme, its objects are $E$-modules with descent isomorphisms. The tensor comparisons in module descent and the canonical affine tilde tensor isomorphism identify multiplication $B\otimes_EB\to B$ and unit $E\to B$ on the two sides. Fullness descends these maps; faithfulness on the triple tensor product and on the unit shows that associativity, commutativity and both unit equations descend. Conversely restriction gives these maps and equations. Thus quasi-coherent algebras are exactly commutative $E$-algebras equipped with algebra descent isomorphisms; their morphisms are exactly the compatible algebra maps.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), applied to multiplication and unit; schemes.tex Tags 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent) and 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions)

proof.text: Reparametrize the arrows by $x\xrightarrow{g}x\cdot g$ (the left-action arrow has parameter $g^{-1}$). Its coordinate ring is $L=E\otimes_kH$, with $s^*(e)=e\otimes1$ and $t^*(e)=\rho_E(e)$. Invert the descent isomorphism if needed, writing $\alpha:B\otimes_{E,t^*}L\xrightarrow{\sim}B\otimes_{E,s^*}L=B\otimes_kH$. Define $\rho_B(b)=\alpha(b\otimes1)$. Since $\alpha$ is an $L$-algebra map, this is a $k$-algebra map and its restriction to $E$ is $\rho_E$. Identity pullback gives $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho_B=1$. On composable right arrows $(x,g),(xg,h)$, evaluation of the cocycle on $b\otimes1$ gives respectively $\sum b_{(0)(0)}\otimes b_{(0)(1)}\otimes b_{(1)}$ and $\sum b_{(0)}\otimes\Delta(b_{(1)})$; their equality is precisely coassociativity.

source.place: Tag 03LF (definition-equivariant-module), the affine coordinate calculation for the cocycle

proof.text: Conversely an extending algebra coaction defines $\alpha(b\otimes l)=\rho_B(b)l$. It is balanced because $\rho_B(eb)=\rho_E(e)\rho_B(b)$. Its inverse on pure tensors is $b\otimes h\mapsto\sum b_{(0)}\otimes(1\otimes S(b_{(1)})h)$. The two composites reduce to the identity by coassociativity and the Hopf equations $\sum h_{(1)}S(h_{(2)})=\epsilon(h)1=\sum S(h_{(1)})h_{(2)}$. These Hopf equations are the coordinate form of the group inverse laws. Counit and coassociativity give the identity and cocycle equations by the two expressions in the preceding step. The constructions are inverse because an $L$-linear map out of $B\otimes_{E,t^*}L$ is determined by $b\otimes1$. Compatibility of algebra maps with $\alpha$ is likewise equivalent to compatibility with $\rho_B$.

source.place: Tag 03LF (definition-equivariant-module); inverse transport from the group inverse laws

proof.text: For a map of the corresponding algebras, module descent identifies its ambient sheaf cokernel with the cokernel of its map on the atlas. Affine tilde equivalence preserves cokernels and detects zero objects. Thus the sheaf map is locally surjective exactly when the module map $B\to B'$ has zero cokernel, that is, when its underlying map of algebras is surjective. The preceding coaction calculation already identifies its equivariance condition. This proves both directions of the assertion about surjections, without claiming left exactness on the big fppf site.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), with cokernels computed by module descent

proof.text: A compatible family of sections of $\mathcal B$ is equivalent to an $\mathcal O$-linear map $\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$: it sends $a$ to $ab$, with inverse evaluation at $1$. Module descent identifies these maps with compatible $E$-linear maps $E\to B$. Such a map is uniquely $e\mapsto eb$; compatibility on $1$ says $\rho_B(b)=b\otimes1$, and for every $e$ the same equality follows from $\rho_B(eb)=\rho_E(e)\rho_B(b)$. Therefore its section ring is $B^G$. This bijection preserves addition, multiplication and unit by their formulas on $B$, and is natural in algebra maps. For $B=E$ it gives $E^G$; the structural section of $c\in C$ is $1\otimes c$, which is invariant by the displayed formula for $\rho_E$.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent): apply full faithfulness to maps from the structure module

proof.text: For $C\to C'$ the chart becomes $E'=E\otimes_CC'$ by the same torsor construction. Tensor pullback on affine sections identifies the restricted algebra with $B'=B\otimes_CC'$ and its coaction with $b\otimes c'\mapsto\sum(b_{(0)}\otimes c')\otimes b_{(1)}$. On invariant global sections the restriction is $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. The multiplication, unit, descent isomorphism and inverse all commute with these maps by their formulas on pure tensors; repeated extension gives the same formulas under tensor associativity. This proves compatibility with further scalar extension and all algebra homomorphisms. It does not assert that $B^G\otimes_CC'\to(B\otimes_CC')^G$ is an isomorphism. All arguments used arbitrary modules and algebras, hence impose no finite-generation condition.
